cases.estimand: Shannon entropy of a fixation group's smoothed map: eyesim's continuous ks estimate at an endpoint-inclusive lattice, eyes4s's native discrete estimate on a grid over the frame.
conventions: the entropy step is entropy_from_mass in eyesim and Mass.entropy in eyes4s, and they agree on the same map

eyesim evaluates ks::kde directly (fewer than 500 points) at outdim endpoint-inclusive points, each observation within a 3.7-standard-deviation support box, then normalises and rounds with zapsmall(z, 7)

eyes4s bins fixations into half-open cells of a grid over the scanpath's frame and applies a truncated discrete Gaussian under an explicit edge policy; fixations outside the frame are listed, not smoothed
suggest_sigma clamps against the padded data range; IqrBandwidth clamps against the frame or not at all
eyesim returns NA for one fixation; eyes4s smooths it with an explicit sigma and refuses the IQR suggestion
absolute tolerance 1e-12; 1e-8 per cell and 1e-7 in entropy for eyesim's rounded map against the continuous oracle
cases.independent_case: Six fixations on a 60 by 40 frame with a 6 by 4 output lattice: the decimal entropy of eyesim's own pinned map reproduces eyesim's value at 1e-12; a continuous Gaussian confined to ks's support box at eyesim's evaluation points reproduces every rounded cell to 1e-8 and the entropy to 1e-7; a direct two-dimensional discrete-kernel sum gives the eyes4s native entropy under both edge policies and both weightings. The all-default call (suggest_sigma clamped on the padded range, padded bounds, a 50 by 50 lattice) matches the same continuous oracle to 1e-7.
cases.divergence: The divergence is the estimator's, recorded by the KDE row: eyes4s entropy of eyesim's own density map equals eyesim's density entropy at 1e-12, but FixationEntropy.density smooths with the native discrete Gaussian on cell centres over the frame, not ks at endpoint-inclusive points, so the values differ (by about 0.018 nats here). Fixations outside the frame are listed by index rather than contributing kernel tails. The unclamped IQR bandwidth agrees; eyesim's default clamps to 15% of the padded data range (8.25 here) while the eyes4s clamp uses the frame (7.5). One fixation gives NA in eyesim under both default and explicit sigma; eyes4s gives a finite entropy for an explicit sigma and a typed Bandwidth error for the IQR rule.

methods: sigma vector on a fixation group
cases.estimand: How per-scale entropies become one number when a scale has no mass, when scales arrive out of order, and when scales are weighted.
conventions: eyesim's multiscale mean is mean(ent, na.rm = TRUE), so a scale whose map has no mass is NA and silently leaves the mean
eyes4s cannot hold a massless scale: Intensity.normalised refuses it with DegenerateTotal before any reduction
eyesim keeps the requested sigma order and names values sigma_<s>; eyes4s orders scales ascending and labels each value with its Sigma
fixation_entropy.fixation_group with a sigma vector returns the mean by default and forwards aggregate, so aggregate = "none" returns the per-scale values of the eye_density_multiscale method
eyes4s ScaleReduction.Weighted takes one explicit weight per scale; eyesim has no weights
cases.independent_case: A fourth, all-zero map at sigma 4 beside the three supplied maps: eyesim's per-scale output is NA there and its mean equals the three-map mean exactly. Weights [1, 3] on sigmas 1 and 3 give (H(q) + 3 H(p)) / 4 exactly (1.625 bits), and [1, 3] on the native scales 6 and 12 are checked against the discrete-kernel oracle.
cases.divergence: eyesim drops a massless (NA) scale from its mean without notice; eyes4s refuses the scale at normalisation, so every reported mean is over every requested scale. eyesim reports scales in request order; eyes4s in ascending sigma, labelled, and the labelled values agree. A sigma vector on a fixation group with aggregate = "none" gives the same per-scale values as the multiscale object, and eyes4s agrees with them by sigma label. Weighted reduction is an eyes4s extension checked against its oracle only.
